answer: A claim becomes an identity only when its proof garden passes panels of strangers: the applicant plants a garden — work samples, an onyx seal, a walnut ledger — and the registry draws five established members at random to inspect it, each sealing a verdict in a walnut shell, cracked only when all five are in. Each co-signer locks a $10 onyx stake, slashed if the identity later proves fake, and may sign one claim per epoch. One applicant's k-th identity needs k such panels. Forging 1,000 puppets takes 5×(1+2+…+1,000) stakes, $25,025,000; an honest applicant needs one panel, $50.
